title: Connelly–Whiteley vertex-splitting conjecture for 3-circuits and global rigidity
statement: Consider a vertex splitting in a three-dimensional framework, with both the added vertex and the split vertex at least $4$-valent. **Connelly–Whiteley vertex-splitting conjecture.** Such a vertex splitting preserves the generic rigidity of $3$-circuits and preserves global rigidity in $3$-space. The source presents this as an open direction following the established two-dimensional analogue.
source_name: Wendy Finbow-Singh and Walter Whiteley, “Isostatic Block and Hole Frameworks”, arXiv:1007.0965 (2010).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.0965

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2010).

title: Symmetry-preserving contraction conjecture for block and hole polyhedra
statement: Let an abstract block and hole polyhedron have graph symmetry group $\Phi(\mathcal{S})$, with no vertices or edges fixed. **Symmetry-preserving contraction conjecture.** There is a symmetry-preserving set of contractions to a base polyhedron realized with the same symmetry group $\mathcal{S}$, again with no vertices or edges fixed; if the base polyhedron is isostatic in some symmetric realization, then the expanded block and hole polyhedron is isostatic when realized generically within the symmetries $\mathcal{S}$. This is proposed as a sufficient mechanism for transferring isostaticity while preserving symmetry; the source warns that fixed vertices or edges can obstruct symmetric vertex-splitting sequences.
source_name: Wendy Finbow-Singh and Walter Whiteley, “Isostatic Block and Hole Frameworks”, arXiv:1007.0965 (2010).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.0965

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2010).

title: Vertex-splitting conjecture for circuits and global rigidity in 3-space
statement: Consider vertex splitting in a three-dimensional framework, with both the added vertex and the split vertex at least $4$-valent. **Vertex-splitting circuit conjecture.** The operation preserves circuits and global rigidity in $3$-space. The source motivates this by the known two-dimensional result, but leaves the three-dimensional assertion as a question.
source_name: Wendy Finbow-Singh and Walter Whiteley, “Isostatic Block and Hole Frameworks”, arXiv:1007.0965 (2010).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.0965

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2010).

title: Vertex-splitting conjecture for smallest non-diregular geodetic digraphs
statement:
A $(d,k,+\epsilon)$-digraph is a digraph with minimum out-degree at least $d$, diameter parameter $k$, and excess $\epsilon$. A **geodetic cage** is a $(d,k,+\epsilon)$-digraph with smallest possible excess, and the **vertex splitting construction** splits a vertex of a digraph into two vertices by duplicating its out-neighborhood and redirecting incident arcs.

**Vertex-splitting conjecture.** All smallest possible non-diregular $(d,k,+\epsilon)$-digraphs can be derived from a diregular $(d,k)$-geodetic cage by the vertex splitting construction.

The conjecture proposes that the vertex-splitting construction accounts for every smallest non-diregular example. The surrounding discussion establishes only that the order of such an example exceeds that of a geodetic cage by at most one; the proposed structural characterization remains open.
source_name: James Tuite, “Digraphs with degree two and excess two are diregular”, arXiv:1703.08739 (2019).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.08739

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

title: Global rigidity conjecture for graphs containing triangulations of surfaces
statement: Let $G$ be a graph with a triangulation $T$ of a surface $S$ as a spanning subgraph. A graph is **globally rigid** when its generic realization is uniquely determined, up to Euclidean isometry, by its edge lengths. **Global rigidity conjecture for triangulated surfaces.** The graph $G$ is globally rigid if and only if $G$ is $4$-connected and, when $S$ has genus zero, $G\neq T$. The conjecture extends the planar triangulation result to arbitrary surfaces. It appeared previously as a question and has been verified when $S$ is the sphere, projective plane, or torus; the general case remains open.
source_name: James Cruickshank, Bill Jackson and Shin-ichi Tanigawa, “Vertex Splitting, Coincident Realisations and Global Rigidity of Braced Triangulations”, arXiv:2002.08680 (2022).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2010–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1010.3605](https://arxiv.org/abs/1010.3605).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.08680

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2020).

title: Vertex-splitting conjecture for global rigidity
statement: Let $G$ be a graph, let $d$ be a positive integer, and let $uv\in E(G)$. Suppose that $G$ is $(d+1)$-connected, $|N_G(u)\cap N_G(v)|=d-1$, and $G/uv$ is globally rigid in $\mathbb R^d$. **Vertex-splitting conjecture.** Then $G$ is globally rigid in $\mathbb R^d$. This is a long-standing question concerning whether the connectivity condition necessary for global rigidity is sufficient in the setting of vertex splitting; the source notes recent developments but does not establish the conjecture.
source_name: James Cruickshank, Bill Jackson and Shin-ichi Tanigawa, “Global Rigidity of Triangulated Manifolds”, arXiv:2204.02503 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.02503

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2022).

title: The one-discus global-rigidity conjecture for discus-and-hole graphs
statement:
Let $G^\dagger$ be a **discus-and-hole graph** with exactly one discus. A framework is **generically globally rigid** in $\mathbb R^3$ when generic realizations are uniquely determined up to Euclidean isometries by their edge lengths, and a graph is **redundantly rigid** in $\mathbb R^3$ when it remains rigid after the deletion of any one edge.

**One-discus global-rigidity conjecture.** The graph $G^\dagger$ is generically globally rigid in $\mathbb R^3$ if and only if it is $4$-connected and redundantly rigid in $\mathbb R^3$.

This is motivated by the known difficulty of global rigidity and by a conjecture of Connelly and Whiteley on vertex splitting. The corresponding vertex-splitting conjecture is still open, although it has been verified in special cases; the proposed characterization for discus-and-hole graphs is therefore open.
source_name: Bryan Gin-ge Chen, James Cruickshank and Derek Kitson, “Block-and-hole graphs: Constructibility and (3,0)-sparsity”, arXiv:2309.06804 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.06804

Status: **open** according to the source (as of September 2023). “This conjecture is still open but has been verified in certain special cases (see ) leading to global rigidity characterisations for braced plane triangulations and for triangulations of non-spherical surfaces.”

title: Hilton–Zhao's vertex-splitting conjecture
statement: Let $G^*$ be an $n$-vertex connected class 1 $\Delta$-regular graph with $\Delta>\frac{n}{3}$. A **vertex-splitting** replaces a vertex by two adjacent vertices whose neighborhoods partition the original neighborhood into two nonempty subsets; suppose $G$ is obtained from $G^*$ in this way. **Vertex-splitting conjecture.** Then $G$ is $\Delta$-critical. Hilton and Zhao proposed this conjecture in 1997. It has been verified in several denser cases, including $\Delta\geq \frac{3(n-1)}{4}$, while the full range $\Delta>\frac{n}{3}$ remains open.
source_name: Yonglei Chen and Yan Cao, “Short Brooms in Edge-chromatic Critical Graphs”, arXiv:2512.07252 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.07252

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).
